original.reason: The converse constructs a nondecreasing extended-valued function on a general metric space, not the required continuous strictly increasing finite function μ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) for the stated interval problem. It also has unsupported supremum/limit details. Additionally, the exact stated inequality at s=t invokes μ(0), outside its declared domain.

judgment.reason: The asserted construction of a continuous strictly increasing majorant is only a vague sketch; the proposed interpolation from values at r_n does not by itself ensure domination of ω throughout every interval. It also applies μ(|x-y|) when x=y although μ is defined only on (0,∞).

The key majorant-existence step is asserted without a valid construction or proof that the interpolant dominates ω on each whole interval. The proof also evaluates μ(0) in the x=y case, outside its domain.

Calling the majorant statement an elementary fact and giving only unsuitable-point interpolation does not rigorously establish it; domination between the selected points is not shown. The final inequality also evaluates μ(0) when x=y.

The claimed standard interpolation is not justified and does not show that μ majorizes ω on all radii, rather than merely at selected radii. It also uses μ(|x-y|) for x=y although μ has no value at 0.
